DESCRIPTION: Axles from the untempered trial group broke in the three-point bending test at low force. Fracture surface flat and shiny with river patterns, typical cleavage. Hardness at the top of the range. Suspect as-quenched martensite without temper.
Same behaviour as the untempered reference group on the Friulpress line: low bending force, brittle fracture. Press itself not the cause, both presses show the same result without tempering.
After 180 C for 1 h tempering, ductility still below target in several lots. SEM shows mixed fracture with large cleavage areas. Tempering temperature probably too low for this carbon level.

First lots with the new 7.8 mm diameter. Bending force lower than on 8 mm parts at the same temper. Drawing change confirmed, test fixture span not adapted to the new diameter. Measurement issue, not material.

Hardness spread between min and max HV10 above 40 points on two samples. Indentation close to the edge on one sample, re-test inside the valid area gave normal values. Operator retrained on indent spacing.
240 C for 1 h gives the best ductility in Version 6 but sits right at the 30 percent target. Request to evaluate longer or series tempering to gain margin.

Series tempering lots from the Freund press: furnace record does not contain the tempering temperature. Results are good but the process cannot be audited. Furnace data logger to be connected to the MES.
Series temper 200 C for 3 h gives the same ductility as 200 C for 1 h in Version 6. Longer time at 200 C adds no benefit, energy cost higher.
Second temper at 220 C after the 200 C series temper improves ductility only to the level of a single 220 C temper. Double tempering not justified for this grade.

X46CrS13 bar stock with higher sulphur: elongated manganese sulphide stringers found at the crack origin in two failed axles. Supplier certificate within limits. Review free-machining grade for the bending-critical variant.
Vacuum hardening trial with 230 C: highest ductility of all campaigns and clean dimple fracture in SEM. Hardness slightly lower but above 600 HV10. Candidate for series release.
Re-tempering at 230 C for 1 h after vacuum hardening: hardness and ductility unchanged within scatter. Extra furnace step under review for removal to save cycle time.
Die-cast housing variant: after overmoulding, two axles show micro-cracks at the press-fit zone. Heat input from casting may re-temper the surface locally. Thermal simulation requested.

Customer return: one axle cracked in end-of-line test. Batch traced to a furnace run where the 240 C temper was interrupted after 25 minutes due to a power fault. Batch was released by mistake; containment of the remaining parts done.
Data platform shows 3-sample lots used for a release decision on the 7.8 mm variant. Procedure requires 5 samples. Test plan in the LIMS to be corrected and the release repeated.
